Python API reference

The package exports mlx.Mlx. Its methods are a thin wrapper over the MinilibX C library documented in src/mlx.h. Return codes from native functions are passed through, typically as 0 on success. Calls that produce a native pointer return None when creation fails.

class mlx.Mlx

Thin ctypes wrapper exposing every function documented in mlx.h.

Load the MLX shared library shipped alongside this module.

mlx_hook(win_ptr, x_event, x_mask, callback, param)

Register a hook for a raw (X11-numbered) event on a window.

Unlike the convenience hooks above, the callback’s arity depends on x_event: key events get (keycode, param), button events get (button, x, y, param), motion events get (x, y, param), anything else gets just (param,).

  • x_mask (int)

  • param (object)

Return type:

Type:

Callback signatures

The callback aliases below are available from mlx.mlx and describe the convenience hook methods:

  • MouseCallback: (button, x, y, param)

  • KeyCallback: (keycode, param)

  • NoArgCallback: (param,); used by expose and loop hooks

  • HookCallback: generic callback for Mlx.mlx_hook(); its arguments depend on the event number

The generic hook uses raw X11 event numbers: key events 2 and 3 receive (keycode, param), button events 4 and 5 receive (button, x, y, param), and motion event 6 receives (x, y, param). Other event numbers receive (param,). Event masks are backend dependent.

Image pixel data

mlx_get_data_addr returns a writable view into the native image buffer. Use size_line to find the start of each row; rows may include padding, so do not assume the stride is width * bytes_per_pixel. The returned format is 0 for B8G8R8A8 or 1 for A8R8G8B8. The view remains tied to the native image and must not be used after mlx_destroy_image.

For mlx_pixel_put and mlx_string_put, the color is an unsigned integer. On little-endian systems, the documented byte order corresponds to 0xAARRGGBB; the integer representation differs on big-endian systems.

Synchronization commands

Use Mlx.mlx_sync() with one of the Mlx.SYNC_* constants:

  • SYNC_IMAGE_WRITABLE (1): wait until an image can be written again.

  • SYNC_WIN_FLUSH (2): wait until pending window requests are sent.

  • SYNC_WIN_COMPLETED (3): wait until pending requests are sent and completed.

mlx_do_sync flushes requests for all windows. On the AppKit backend, a frame is shown only while mlx_loop pumps the native event loop; a sync call alone does not display it.
